chunks: And from him, from his father, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Aban and Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When you stand for the prayer, say: O Allah! I present Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) before my need, and I turn to You through him, so make me esteemed through Him in Your presence in this world and the Hereafter, and of those who are brought near. Make my prayer acceptable through him, and my sin forgiven through him, and my supplication answered through him. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when standing for prayer according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This supplication, recorded in Al-Kafi, emphasizes the Shia concept of *tawassul* by positioning the Prophet Muhammad as an intercessor to secure acceptance of prayer and forgiveness. It reflects the theological belief that spiritual proximity (*wajh*) to God is achieved through the Prophet, linking earthly worship with eternal elevation among the *muqarrabin* (those brought near to God).
